articleBody:
Getting an estimate for kitchen drywall repair goes smoother when you know what is happening behind the surface. Here is a practical checklist of what to check and note before a contractor visits:

- [ ] Check beneath the kitchen sink for active water drips — You need to know whether an active supply or drain leak is still dampening the wall framing.
- [ ] Inspect adjacent cabinetry for swelling or separation — Water wicked up into cabinet boxes changes the overall scope of the wall repair.
- [ ] Measure the visible square footage of water staining — Accurate dimensions give your contractor a clear starting point for drywall removal.
- [ ] Look closely for dark spotting or surface mold — Mildew or mold inside damp wall cavities indicates a need for deeper removal rather than a simple patch.
- [ ] Tap the drywall gently to check for spongy or crumbling spots — Soft board means moisture has degraded the gypsum core beyond cosmetic repair.
- [ ] Check if the damage sits near gas lines or kitchen wiring — Knowing utility locations helps plan safe cutting and clean structural framing.
- [ ] Note down the age of the home — Older homes may require specific handling if coatings or building materials could contain hazardous components.
- [ ] Clear a three-foot work zone around the damaged area — Providing direct physical access allows your contractor to inspect the wall cavity accurately on day one.

How to use this checklist
Go through these points before your consultation so you can point out specific problem spots and leak histories. Sharing these details right away helps your contractor determine if you just need a straightforward sheet patch or structural drywall replacement.
